title: Aerated Venezuelan Flour Empanadas
description: Cultured, aerated version of Venezuelan empanadas ideal for a date-night dinner. Served hot with a dollop of cream.

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.notes: Use a high-protein flour for best results

ingredients.name: Shio-cure salmon (optional)
ingredients.notes: Cured in sea salt, sugar, and spices for 2 weeks

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add more if dough is too dry

ingredients.name: Bread flour
ingredients.notes: Added to enhance structure and aeration

instructions: Combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix buttermilk, lard or shortening, and egg.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let it rest in a warm place for 1 hour.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 8-10 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten it slightly into a disk shape.
Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each disk and fold the dough over to form a half-moon shape.
Press the edges together to seal the empanada and cut a few slits in the top to allow steam to escape.
Brush the tops with a little water and bake in a preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown.
